fixes.explanation: Joshua doesn't come up in this passage at all. The man says, “Your name will no longer be Jacob, but Israel…” (Genesis 32:28). That's the name Jacob walks away with. Joshua can sit this one out, like a cookie that never made it onto the tray.

Making peace with Esau would be a lovely ending, but this passage doesn't give it. Esau is Jacob's twin brother (Genesis 25:24–26), and he isn't mentioned in these verses. That's like putting sprinkles on a cookie before it's even baked. Jacob's reason for the name is, “Indeed, I have seen God face to face, and yet my life was spared.” (Genesis 32:30).

That's the reason the text gives, baker. “…the Israelites do not eat the tendon attached to the socket of the hip, because the socket of Jacob’s hip was struck near that tendon.” (Genesis 32:32). The verse starts with “Therefore to this day…” so the habit was still going when this was written. One night at the river, and a whole people remembers it at the table. I can't keep a New Year's resolution past February, and this habit outlasted all of mine.

Priests get plenty of mentions in the Bible, but this verse isn't one of them. The text gives its reason: “…because the socket of Jacob’s hip was struck near that tendon.” (Genesis 32:32). That tendon doesn't have a job title here. It has a memory, and the memory goes back to Jacob's hip at the Jabbok.

Bowstrings! Now that's a plot twist, and I respect the imagination, friend. But the text never mentions them. It says the Israelites do not eat that tendon “…because the socket of Jacob’s hip was struck near that tendon.” (Genesis 32:32). The reason goes back to Jacob and that night at the Jabbok, no archery involved.
